title: ZuriQ and Rhonexum Form Multi-Year Partnership to Integrate Cryogenic Control ICs into 2D Trapped-Ion Processors - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Swiss trapped-ion startup ZuriQ (ETH Zurich spin-out, 2024) signed a multi-year framework agreement with EPFL spin-out Rhonexum (2025) to integrate cryogenic control ICs into its 2D reconfigurable ion-trap processors, with the first hardware shipment due by end-2026 followed by co-designed ASICs. The deal targets the I/O wiring bottleneck that makes room-temperature control lines unviable as 2D trapped-ion arrays scale to thousands of qubits.

insights.claim: ZuriQ and Rhonexum signed a multi-year commercial framework agreement under which Rhonexum supplies cryogenic integrated circuits and customization engineering services for ZuriQ's trapped-ion hardware, with the first hardware shipment scheduled for deployment by the end of 2026.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Concrete supply deal with a dated delivery milestone; track whether the end-2026 shipment lands.
insights.quote: the inaugural hardware shipment scheduled for deployment by the end of 2026
insights.locator: Under the agreement, Rhonexum will deliver

insights.claim: After the initial delivery of Rhonexum's control hardware in late 2026, the partnership moves to co-designed ASICs, with ZuriQ's operational trapped-ion performance metrics feeding back into Rhonexum's cryogenic semiconductor modeling tools.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Co-design loop signals vertical integration of control electronics, a moat-building step for trapped-ion scaling.

insights.claim: Both companies are young academic spin-outs: ZuriQ came out of Professor Jonathan Home's lab at ETH Zurich in 2024 and Rhonexum from EPFL's AQUA Lab in 2025, and the deal is framed as translating Swiss university research into a domestic quantum hardware supply chain.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Switzerland is building a local quantum supply chain; early-stage private-market names to watch rather than public plays.
insights.locator: Spun out of Professor Jonathan Home

themes.theme: Wiring bottleneck in scaling trapped-ion systems

insights.claim: As trapped-ion architectures scale from tens to thousands of physical qubits, routing individual room-temperature RF and DC control lines into cryogenic vacuum chambers creates prohibitive thermal loads, footprint constraints and interconnect bottlenecks.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Control I/O, not qubit physics alone, is a gating constraint on trapped-ion scale-up; suppliers solving it gain leverage.

insights.claim: Direct coax and multi-pin feedthrough wiring between 300 K racks and the cryostat is manageable for linear chains of 10 to 50 ions but becomes unviable for high-density 2D arrays, where electrode density scales quadratically.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Explains why 2D trapped-ion roadmaps require cryo-CMOS-style electronics, a parallel to superconducting qubit wiring challenges.
insights.quote: this direct-wiring approach becomes unviable for high-density 2D arrays, where electrode density scales quadratically

insights.claim: ZuriQ's processor uses a natively two-dimensional, reconfigurable ion-trap architecture combining static magnetic and dynamic electric fields, targeting thousands of physical qubits.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Differentiated 2D trap design versus linear-chain incumbents; scaling claims remain targets, not demonstrations.
insights.locator: Spun out of Professor Jonathan Home

insights.claim: Rhonexum designs semiconductor ICs that operate directly at sub-Kelvin and 4-Kelvin cryogenic stages, enabling localized signal routing, digital multiplexing and waveform generation close to the qubits.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Cryo-IC is an enabling layer across modalities; a picks-and-shovels angle in quantum hardware.
insights.locator: Spun out of EPFL's AQUA Lab

insights.claim: Moving analog voltage DACs, fast switching electronics and multiplexing ICs to the cryogenic stage aims to sharply cut physical vacuum feedthroughs per qubit while preserving shuttle fidelity, individual addressing and dynamic reconfigurability.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Success would be measured by feedthroughs-per-qubit and fidelity retention; watch for published metrics.
